generationContext.text:
# Microsoft Azure Database Migration management client library for .NET

Microsoft Azure Database Migration Service is a tool that helps you simplify, guide, and automate your database migration to Azure. Easily migrate your data, schema, and objects from multiple sources to the cloud at scale.

This library supports managing Microsoft Azure Database Migration resources.

This library follows the [new Azure SDK guidelines](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/general_introduction.html), and provides many core capabilities:

    - Support MSAL.NET, Azure.Identity is out of box for supporting MSAL.NET.
    - Support [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) for distributed tracing.
    - HTTP pipeline with custom policies.
    - Better error-handling.
    - Support uniform telemetry across all languages.

## Getting started 

### Install the package

Install the Microsoft Azure Database Migration management library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.ResourceManager.DataMigration
```

### Prerequisites

* You must have an [Microsoft Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/).

### Authenticate the Client

To create an authenticated client and start interacting with Microsoft Azure resources, see the [quickstart guide here](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).

## Key concepts

Key concepts of the Microsoft Azure SDK for .NET can be found [here](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html).

## Documentation

Documentation is available to help you learn how to use this package:

- [Quickstart](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/doc/dev/mgmt_quickstart.md).
- [API References](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/?view=azure-dotnet).
- [Authentication](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md).

## Examples

Code samples for using the management library for .NET can be found in the following locations
- [.NET Management Library Code Samples](https://aka.ms/azuresdk-net-mgmt-samples)

## Troubleshooting

-   File an issue via [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/issues).
-   Check [previous questions](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/tagged/azure+.net) or ask new ones on Stack Overflow using Azure and .NET tags.

## Next steps

For more information about Microsoft Azure SDK, see [this website](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/).

## Contributing

For details on contributing to this repository, see the [contributing
guide][cg].

This project welcomes contributions and suggestions. Most contributions
require you to agree to a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) declaring
that you have the right to, and actually do, grant us the rights to use
your contribution. For details, visit <https://cla.microsoft.com>.

When you submit a pull request, a CLA-bot will automatically determine
whether you need to provide a CLA and decorate the PR appropriately
(for example, label, comment). Follow the instructions provided by the
bot. You'll only need to do this action once across all repositories
using our CLA.

This project has adopted the [Microsoft Open Source Code of Conduct][coc]. For
more information, see the [Code of Conduct FAQ][coc_faq] or contact
<opencode@microsoft.com> with any other questions or comments.

proposals.subtype: Debug-conditional collection validator allowing server or resource-group scope
proposals.explanation: CodeGenSuppress targets ValidateResourceId. The replacement internal static method has Conditional("DEBUG") and permits Microsoft.Sql/servers or Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups, throwing ArgumentException for other types. Its error text names only servers despite the two allowed types. Conditional call-site compilation prevents treating it as an unconditional release-mode guard.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Customization partial explicitly suppresses the generated validator name and supplies a concrete replacement body with a two-type predicate.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete SQL DB migration creation overloads rebinding collection scope
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete CreateOrUpdate sync/async overloads use GetCompatCollection(sqlDBInstanceName), then forward waitUntil, targetDBName, data and cancellation. The helper reuses this for an existing Microsoft.Sql/servers parent; otherwise it constructs a collection with Client and a server ID interpolated from Id.SubscriptionId, Id.ResourceGroupName and the supplied server name. On the reuse branch the supplied server name is not consulted.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Customization implements explicit deprecated public adapters and concrete collection-scope rebinding outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete SQL DB migration existence overloads adapting parent scope
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete Exists pair selects the current server-scoped collection or builds a server-scoped collection from subscription/resource-group state and sqlDBInstanceName. It then forwards targetDBName, nullable Guid migrationOperationId, expand and cancellation unchanged to the corresponding existence overload; bool response interpretation is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Concrete parent-scope adaptation and deprecated overload bodies appear in Customization outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete SQL DB migration retrieval overloads adapting parent scope
proposals.explanation: Get/GetAsync use the shared selector to reuse a server-scoped collection or create one from the stored subscription/resource group and supplied sqlDBInstanceName. They forward targetDBName, migrationOperationId, expand and cancellation to the corresponding retrieval overload, returning its typed response/Task directly.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Customization supplies explicit hidden obsolete scope-adapting retrieval overloads.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete optional SQL DB migration retrieval overloads adapting scope
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete GetIfExists sync/async methods select or construct the server-scoped collection through GetCompatCollection and forward targetDBName, nullable migrationOperationId, expand and cancellation to the corresponding NullableResponse-shaped overload. No missing-resource detection logic is implemented in these wrappers.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The Customization partial implements explicit deprecated overload and parent-scope adaptation bodies.

proposals.subtype: Debug-conditional collection validator allowing managed-instance or group scope
proposals.explanation: The Customization partial suppresses ValidateResourceId and provides a Conditional("DEBUG") replacement permitting Microsoft.Sql/managedInstances or Microsoft.Resources/resourceGroups. Other types cause ArgumentException whose message names managedInstances only. Call sites/build symbols are not supplied, so this is not asserted to guard release-mode requests.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit generator suppression and a concrete replacement type-checking implementation establish customization.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete managed-instance migration creation overloads rebinding scope
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete CreateOrUpdate pair reuses this when Id.ResourceType is Microsoft.Sql/managedInstances; otherwise its helper constructs a collection with Client and a managedInstances ID from the stored subscription/resource group and managedInstanceName. It forwards waitUntil, targetDBName, data and cancellation. The already-bound branch does not inspect the supplied managed-instance name.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Customization supplies explicit deprecated public wrappers and concrete parent-scope selection/construction.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete managed-instance migration existence overloads adapting scope
proposals.explanation: Hidden Exists/ExistsAsync wrappers obtain the existing managed-instance-scoped collection or build one using managedInstanceName and stored subscription/group state. They forward targetDBName, nullable Guid migrationOperationId, expand and cancellation without parsing/converting the Guid or implementing bool response handling.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Explicit scope-adapting hidden obsolete wrappers are implemented in Customization outside Generated.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete managed-instance migration retrieval overloads adapting scope
proposals.explanation: Get/GetAsync select or construct a managed-instance-scoped collection through the shown helper, then forward targetDBName, migrationOperationId, expand and cancellation to the corresponding retrieval overload. The server response and async Task are delegated, not locally transformed.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Customization implements nonempty hidden obsolete public methods and their concrete scope rebinding.

proposals.subtype: Obsolete optional managed-instance migration retrieval scope adapter
proposals.explanation: The hidden obsolete GetIfExists pair selects or constructs the managed-instance collection and forwards targetDBName, nullable migrationOperationId, expand and cancellation to the corresponding optional retrieval overload. The supplied parent name is unused on the already-correctly-scoped branch; missing-resource interpretation is delegated.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: Non-generated Customization source contains explicit deprecated forwarding and parent-scope adaptation.

decisions.reason: The non-generated partial explicitly suppresses ValidateResourceId and implements the cited two-type check. Conditional("DEBUG") limits compiled call sites, so the proposal correctly avoids describing an unconditional release guard. This is input validation, not custom polling.

Both obsolete creation overloads and the shared scope selector are present, but the catalog already calls retained obsolete forwarding overloads legacy-overload-compatibility. Whether a generic generator could preserve these historical, scope-rebinding signatures is unclear from the supplied evidence.

The server-name argument is not used on the already-server-scoped branch; these wrappers do not implement an LRO poller.

limitations: Only two Customization files of 861 eligible files were captured; 28 named Customization paths were skipped. The library inventory is partial.

Comments describe GA resource-group scoping and a code-generation transition. Current adapters/obsolescence are observable, but prior APIs and the generated parent collection behavior are not independently supplied.

Private GetCompatCollection methods are included as shared implementation of their operation-specific public adapters, not counted again. The two explicitly suppressed/replaced validators implement a separate scope-acceptance contract.
Conditional(DEBUG) validators cannot be treated as unconditional production validation. Their call sites, compilation symbols and generated constructor behavior are not supplied.

Parent-name arguments are ignored when the collection is already bound to the expected parent type; otherwise helper strings interpolate the supplied names directly. No name matching, input escaping or additional null/empty validation appears in the shown helper/wrapper bodies, regardless of XML exception documentation.
Migration-operation Guids, expand values and cancellation are forwarded unchanged. No custom Guid parsing, polling, bool conversion or optional-resource error handling is supplied.
Generator addressability means these signatures, scope rules and validation shapes could plausibly be emitted, not that current emitter support or a measured causal explanation has been demonstrated.

Only two of 861 eligible files were captured; 28 customization paths were explicitly skipped. This review covers the supplied two collection files only and neither establishes exhaustive customization discovery nor absence elsewhere.

The source itself shows obsolete methods, but the historical GA signature and reason for retaining it are not independently verified by supplied generated or historical source; source comments are not independent proof.

The implementations of delegated generated methods and validator call sites/build symbols are not supplied. In particular, the wrappers do not establish custom LRO or existence/paging internals, and Conditional("DEBUG") does not prove a release-mode runtime guard.
Decisions are AI-reviewed, not human-verified; no omission is counted as accepted.
